questions.q: Who was the master of Bilal bin Rabah who tortured him?
questions.explain: Umayyah, a millionaire, tortured Bilal because he was ashamed his slave had embraced Islam.

questions.q: What did Bilal keep saying while being tortured, and what does it mean?
questions.explain: Bilal kept saying Ahad, Allah is One, even when whipped in the street.
Abu Bakr paid a high price to free Bilal.

questions.q: What happened to Zinnirah after she said that only Allah has power?
questions.explain: Zinnirah was beaten until she was blind, then Allah restored her sight.

questions.q: What was the job of Khabbab, who was tortured with hot iron?
questions.explain: Khabbab was a blacksmith tortured with hot iron on his back.

questions.q: Who was the first martyr in Islam?
questions.explain: Sumayyah was stabbed by Abu Jahal and became the first martyr.

questions.q: What concession is there for someone forced to utter words of disbelief?
options: It is allowed as a joke
It is allowed if his heart stays firm in faith
questions.explain: Like Ammar, who was forced but whose heart stayed firm. Allah gives a concession.

questions.q: What title did the Prophet SAW give Abu Jahal?
questions.explain: The Arabs called him Abul Hakam, but the Prophet SAW called him the Pharaoh of this nation.

questions.q: Abu Bakr used his wealth to buy luxury goods.
questions.explain: False. He used his wealth to help and free those being tortured.

questions.q: Put these events in the right order.

items.text: Ammar is forced to utter disbelief
Bilal is whipped in the street

questions.explain: Bilal embraced Islam, was whipped, bought by Abu Bakr, then Sumayyah was martyred and Ammar was forced.

questions.q: Match each term with its meaning.

right.text: A person owned by a master and not paid
One who dies defending the faith

questions.explain: Ahad means one, a shahid dies defending the faith, a slave is owned by a master, and Abul Hakam means father of wisdom.

questions.q: We easily say la ilaha illallah today. What is the right attitude?
options: Be grateful, because the early generation sacrificed
questions.explain: The early generation sacrificed so we could say the shahada easily.
